chunks: Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi said in Al-Imta' wa al-Mu'anasa, vol. 1, p. 141:

"As for Ibn al-Mu'allim, he is eloquent of tongue and skilled in dialectical disputation, patient against his opponent, resourceful in stratagems, discreet in secrets, and beautiful in public conduct."
ai.seo_question: What did Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi write about Sheikh al-Mufid (Ibn al-Mu'allim) in Al-Imta' wa al-Mu'anasa?
ai.summary: Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi, the renowned Abbasid litterateur and contemporary of Sheikh al-Mufid, praises Ibn al-Mu'allim — a well-known epithet for Sheikh al-Mufid — in his celebrated work Al-Imta' wa al-Mu'anasa for five qualities: eloquence of tongue and dialectical skill, patience against adversaries, resourcefulness in stratagems, discretion in secrets, and admirable public conduct. This external testimony from a non-Shia intellectual peer is cited in the chapter of praises (āyāt al-thanāʾ) within Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām to establish the broad, cross-sectarian recognition of Sheikh al-Mufid's extraordinary scholarly character.
